messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: P0 - service=redwood-serving-queue-backlog (us-west). Trigger=queue.depth > 2000 for 5m. Affected product: hosted API (text generation). Incident INC-1856001234 created and paged primary on-call. @oncall please acknowledge.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Escalation policy 'eng-oncall' fired — primary paged: Alice Chen. If no ACK within 2m, will escalate to Ben Patel.

Alice Chen: ack — oncall here, looking. thanks for the page. @Maria can you pull queue/deployment metrics and HPA state? tagging @Runtime Eng in case we need immediate scale.

Maria Gonzales: grabbing metrics now. initial read: queue depth 2.7k across prod-us-west, p50 latency ~450ms, 5xx ~6% (mostly 503s). Throughput up, but HPA doesn't seem to be increasing replicas.

Maria Gonzales: paste logs/commands:
```
# prometheus query: service_queue_depth{region="us-west"}
> 2700

# kubectl get hpa -n prod
NAME                     REFERENCE                        TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
redwood-runtime-hpa      Deployment/redwood-runtime        0%/80%    5         50        5          3d
```

Maria Gonzales: HPA shows 0% target (metrics missing). HPA controller logs show metric request errors. suspect metrics-server/custom-metrics adapter is failing.

Runtime Eng: looking at autoscaler logs from last 15m — seeing repeated errors: "failed to get metrics: 500 internal server error from metrics-adapter". snippet:
```
2026-03-14T10:07:12Z autoscaler ERROR failed to query custom metrics: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = adapter timeout
2026-03-14T10:08:05Z autoscaler WARN evaluate: stabilization window preventing scale up? current replicas=5 desired>30
```

Ryan O'Neill: if adapter is down, HPA will think load is 0 and keep pods at min. that matches 0% target. we should scale manually while ops fixes adapter.

Alice Chen: agreed. manual surge to buy us time and reduce customer impact. executing scale and temporary routing fallback.

Ryan O'Neill: commands I'm running now (prod):
```bash
kubectl -n prod scale deployment redwood-runtime --replicas=30
# verify
kubectl -n prod get deploy redwood-runtime -o wide
```

Deploy Bot: deploy-bot: Command accepted, scaling deployment redwood-runtime -> 30 replicas.

Deploy Bot: kubectl output: deployment.apps/redwood-runtime scaled

Maria Gonzales: new pods coming up. monitoring queue depth...

~6m later

Maria Gonzales: queue depth trending down: 2700 -> 900 -> 300. p50 latency back to ~120ms. 5xx down to ~0.8%. partial mitigation achieved.

Alice Chen: good. notifying SRE that we need to restore autoscaler. @Runtime Eng can you triage metrics-adapter? looks like it's returning 500s. might be an auth/token expiry with adapter -> prometheus.

Runtime Eng: investigating. found adapter pods in CrashLoopBackOff on one node; logs show `panic: runtime error` in metrics adapter v1.2.3 after TLS handshake with prometheus. rolling restart to get new image pinned to v1.2.4.

Ryan O'Neill: rolling restart performed: `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/custom-metrics-adapter`

Runtime Eng: adapter back up. HPA now showing targets again. current HPA status:
```
# kubectl get hpa -n prod redwood-runtime-hpa -o yaml
status:
  currentMetrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      currentAverageUtilization: 78
  desiredReplicas: 28
  currentReplicas: 30
```

Maria Gonzales: autoscaler started driving replicas down from manual scale to desired (observed drop to 22 then 15). queue stable at ~150.

Alice Chen: assessing customer impact: hosted API in us-west experienced elevated latency and 503s for ~13m window; estimated 2.4% of active requests affected (based on sampling). Notified support & status page team to post an incident notice for affected customers.

Ben Patel: I'm incoming for 1h handoff. Alice — want me to keep watch and own PD follow-ups?

Alice Chen: thanks Ben — please take on-call handoff. I'll stay available for questions but heading to triage/pm sync. Ben will ACK takeover.

Ben Patel: ack — taking over. monitoring queue and HPA for next 60m. also will open a follow-up ticket to pin adapter image and add liveness probe to prevent crash loops.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident INC-1856001234 status changed -> acknowledged by Alice Chen, assigned to eng-oncall.

~30m later

Maria Gonzales: post-mitigations: final metrics:
- peak queue depth: 2700
- time to manual scale+stabilize: ~18m
- duration of customer impact window: ~13m
- percent requests with 5xx: peak 6%, overall 1.1% during incident

Alice Chen: resolution steps executed:
1) Manual scale to 30 replicas to absorb backlog.
2) Rollout restart of custom-metrics-adapter -> rolled back to stable v1.2.4.
3) HPA resumed normal operation; autoscaler transitioned replicas back to desired range.
4) Notified support & status page.

Alice Chen: root cause (preliminary): custom-metrics-adapter v1.2.3 crashed after TLS edge-case with prometheus client, causing HPA to receive 0% targets and keep replicas at min. autoscaler did not scale up because metrics were missing. manual scale necessary to clear queue.

Alice Chen: next actions (tracked in INC-1856001234 follow-up):
- Owner: Maria Gonzales — pin adapter image to v1.2.4 and add liveness/readiness probes (ETA 24h)
- Owner: Runtime Eng — add alert for metrics-adapter errors (500s) and playbook for manual scale runbook (ETA 48h)
- Postmortem: assigned to Maria, severity P1, draft due in 48 hours.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident INC-1856001234 status changed -> resolved by Alice Chen.

incident-bot: Incident INC-1856001234: RESOLVED — manual mitigation succeeded, autoscaler restored. Postmortem owner: Maria Gonzales.

Ben Patel: thanks team. I'll keep eyes on it for the hour and then rotate. adding notes to the oncall rotation doc. :wave:

Alice Chen: thanks everyone for the quick coordination. filing a short blameless summary for the PMs and ops.

Runtime Eng: quick callout — suggest we add a canary alert that detects HPA target=0 for >2m in prod. flagged in follow-up ticket.

Maria Gonzales: creating follow-up tickets now and attaching logs/graphs.

_end of thread_
